modules.title: Principles of Electrical Engineering: Circuits & Power Conversion
modules.desc: DC and AC circuits, network theorems, AC power, electrical machines (DC, induction, BLDC, stepper, transformer, alternator), power electronics, drives, and electrical safety & earthing.

topics.label: Ohm's Law & Circuit Elements
topics.summary: V=IR links voltage, current and resistance for a single resistor — the atomic building block every other law in this topic is built from.

topics.label: Kirchhoff's Laws (KCL, KVL)
topics.summary: KCL: current into a node equals current out (conservation of charge). KVL: voltage rises equal drops around any closed loop (conservation of energy).

topics.label: Series, Parallel & Dividers
topics.summary: Series resistors share one current and simply add; parallel resistors share one voltage and add as reciprocals. The voltage- and current-divider shortcuts follow directly.

topics.label: Node-Voltage Analysis
topics.summary: Pick a reference node, assign unknown voltages to the rest, write one KCL equation per unknown node, and solve — best for circuits rich in parallel branches.

topics.label: Mesh-Current Analysis
topics.summary: Assign a circulating current to each loop and write one KVL equation per loop; a shared branch carries the difference of its two mesh currents.

topics.label: Source Transformation
topics.summary: A voltage source with series R is externally indistinguishable from a current source I=V/R with the same R in parallel — a useful circuit-simplifying swap.

topics.label: Thevenin's & Norton's Theorem
topics.summary: Any linear network, seen from two terminals, collapses to one source (V_th or I_N) plus one resistance (R_th) — found from the open-circuit voltage and the source-killed resistance.

topics.label: Maximum Power Transfer Theorem
topics.summary: A Thevenin source delivers maximum power to a load when R_L=R_th — derived by differentiating load power with respect to R_L and setting it to zero.

topics.label: Superposition Theorem
topics.summary: In a linear circuit with several independent sources, the total response is the sum of each source's individual contribution, with all other sources killed in turn.

topics.label: Generating an AC Waveform
topics.summary: A coil rotating at constant speed in a uniform field produces v(t)=V_m sin(ωt) — the rotating-coil picture behind every AC quantity that follows.

topics.label: RMS, Average, Form Factor & Peak Factor
topics.summary: RMS (V_m/√2) and half-cycle average (2V_m/π) are both derived by integration; their ratio gives the form factor, and V_m/V_rms gives the peak factor.

topics.label: Phasors & Impedance
topics.summary: A phasor freezes a sinusoid's magnitude and phase as a complex number; impedance Z=R+jX generalises resistance so KVL/KCL algebra keeps working unchanged for AC.

topics.label: Series RL, RC, RLC Circuits
topics.summary: Impedance triangles for RL (lagging), RC (leading) and RLC (either, or resonant when X_L=X_C) circuits, with |Z|, phase angle and current computed directly.

topics.label: Power & Power Factor in AC Circuits
topics.summary: Real power P=VIcosφ, reactive power Q=VIsinφ and apparent power S=VI form a right triangle (S²=P²+Q²); power factor cosφ=P/S governs how much current is needed for a given useful watt.

topics.label: Energy & Electricity-Bill Calculations
topics.summary: Energy = power × time, the kWh 'unit', and working out a household bill from appliance ratings.

topics.label: DC Motor: Construction
topics.summary: Every part explained — yoke, poles and pole shoes, armature core/winding (lap vs wave), commutator, brushes — with material, purpose and why the iron is laminated.

topics.label: DC Motor: Working Principle & Back EMF
topics.summary: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule gives force direction (F=BIL); the moving conductor also generates a back-EMF (V=E_b+I_aR_a), which is why a starter is needed. Includes the DC generator principle (8 loop positions, commutation).

topics.label: Types of DC Motors
topics.summary: Separately excited, shunt, series and short/long-shunt compound — circuit equations, characteristics and applications — plus DC generator types and their uses.

topics.label: Transformer: Construction
topics.summary: Working principle (mutual induction), laminated core, core-type vs shell-type windings, ideal-transformer ratios, losses and applications.

topics.label: Transformer: EMF Equation
topics.summary: Faraday's law on a sinusoidal flux gives E=4.44fΦ_mN — the same √2 conversion from B2's RMS derivation reappears here as the constant 4.44.

topics.label: Three-Phase Induction Motor
topics.summary: Stator construction, why three phases make a rotating field (N_s=120f/P), slip, squirrel-cage vs wound rotor (full comparison table) and applications.

topics.label: Single-Phase Induction Motor
topics.summary: Why a single-phase induction motor cannot start by itself, and the five starting methods (split-phase, capacitor-start, CSCR, PSC, shaded-pole).

topics.label: BLDC Motor (Brushless DC)
topics.summary: Permanent-magnet rotor, stator coils switched electronically in a six-step sequence; no brushes or commutator.

topics.label: Stepper Motor
topics.summary: A motor that turns in fixed steps for each pulse — precise position control without feedback.

topics.label: Alternator (Synchronous Generator)
topics.summary: Stationary armature + rotating field: how an AC generator makes three-phase power at a fixed frequency.

topics.label: Concepts of Power Electronics
topics.summary: Switching devices that convert and control electrical power: rectifier, inverter, chopper; PWM and efficiency.

topics.label: Industrial Applications of Electrical Drives
topics.summary: An electric drive = source + power converter + motor + load with sensing and control; VFDs for speed control of pumps, fans, robots, EVs.

topics.label: Earthing
topics.summary: Earthing gives fault current a low-resistance path to the ground; plate, rod and pipe earthing; earthing vs grounding.

topics.label: Electrical Hazards & Safety
topics.summary: Shock, burns, arc, explosion, fire; effect of current levels; the five ways accidents are prevented.

modules.title: Foundations of Electronics & Communication Systems
modules.desc: PN, Zener, BJT and MOSFET; rectifiers and voltage regulators; op-amps; the EM spectrum; communication systems, cellular, satellite and radar.

topics.label: PN Junction Diode
topics.summary: P and N regions, the depletion layer and barrier potential, forward/reverse bias, the diode equation and silicon vs germanium.

topics.label: Zener Diode
topics.summary: A heavily doped diode designed to operate in reverse breakdown as a voltage reference.

topics.label: Voltage Regulator (Zener shunt regulator)
topics.summary: Series resistor + Zener across the load to hold a constant DC output despite supply or load changes.

topics.label: Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT)
topics.summary: Three-layer NPN/PNP device; α, β, the CB/CE/CC configurations and characteristics.

topics.label: MOSFET
topics.summary: Voltage-controlled transistor with an insulated gate; enhancement vs depletion, regions of operation, BJT vs MOSFET.

topics.label: Rectifiers
topics.summary: Half-wave, centre-tap full-wave and bridge rectifiers; I<sub>dc</sub>, I<sub>rms</sub>, efficiency, ripple and PIV.

topics.label: Operational Amplifiers
topics.summary: Ideal op-amp properties, virtual earth, inverting, non-inverting and summing amplifiers.

topics.label: Electromagnetic Spectrum
topics.summary: The full range of EM radiation from radio to gamma; c = fλ and E = hf.

topics.label: Elements of a Communication System
topics.summary: Source, transducers, transmitter, channel, noise, receiver, destination; why modulation is needed.

topics.label: Overview of Cellular Communication
topics.summary: Cells, base stations, frequency reuse, handoff and the generations of mobile networks.

topics.label: Fundamentals of Satellite Communication
topics.summary: Uplink/downlink, transponder, orbits (LEO, MEO, GEO) and delay.

topics.label: Fundamentals of Radar
topics.summary: Radio detection and ranging: range from echo time, Doppler for speed.

modules.title: Engineering Graphics & CAD
modules.desc: BIS standards, orthographic projection (first/third angle), projection of solids, isometric and perspective, freehand sketching, building drawing, CAD — plus the CAT-1 question patterns.

topics.label: Engineering Drawing: Importance & Scope
topics.summary: Drawing as the language of engineers, what it is used for, and the move from drawing boards to CAD.

topics.label: Drawing Sheets, Scales & Title Block
topics.summary: A-series sheet sizes (A0–A4), the title block and what it records.

topics.label: Types of Lines
topics.summary: BIS line types A–K and what each is used for in orthographic drawing; pencil grades.

topics.label: Lettering & Dimensioning
topics.summary: Single-stroke capital lettering; elements and systems of dimensioning; chain vs parallel.

topics.label: Dimensioning Rules & Checking Errors
topics.summary: Rules for placing dimensions correctly, with the CAT-1 'identify the dimensioning errors' question.

topics.label: Orthographic Projection: Principles, First & Third Angle
topics.summary: Planes of projection, the four quadrants, first- vs third-angle layout and symbols.

topics.label: Drawing Orthographic Views: Method & Worked Examples
topics.summary: Steps for converting a pictorial view to FV, TV and LSV, with the CAT-1 style question.

topics.label: Projection of Solids
topics.summary: Front and top views of prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones in simple positions; CAT-1 pyramid.

topics.label: Isometric Projection
topics.summary: Isometric axes, isometric scale (0.816), isometric drawing vs projection, circles and the CAT-1 cylinder.

topics.label: Freehand Sketching
topics.summary: Why and how to sketch lines, circles and orthographic views by hand.

topics.label: Perspective Projection
topics.summary: How a picture plane image of an object looks to an observer: terms, types, visual-ray method.

topics.label: Introduction to Building Drawing (Floor Plan)
topics.summary: Plan, elevation and section; BIS conventions; a simple residential floor plan.

topics.label: Introduction to CAD
topics.summary: What CAD is, 2-D sketching vs 3-D solid modelling, common features, file types and the CAD→CAM link.

topics.label: CAT-1 Pattern — What the Paper Asked
topics.summary: The CAT-1 question types (Module 3 and casting) and where to revise each.

modules.title: Manufacturing, Energy Conversion & Mechanical Automation
modules.desc: Casting, forming, joining, machining, CNC and 3-D printing; IC engines, power plants, refrigeration, fuel cells; mechanisms, mechanical components, robotics and pneumatic/hydraulic actuators.

topics.label: Metal Casting
topics.summary: Pouring molten metal into a mould: sand casting steps, pattern allowances (CAT-1 Q5), types and defects.

topics.label: Forming Processes
topics.summary: Shaping by plastic deformation: forging, rolling, extrusion, drawing and sheet-metal operations.

topics.label: Joining Processes
topics.summary: Welding (arc, gas, resistance), soldering, brazing, riveting, adhesives.

topics.label: Cutting (Machining) Processes
topics.summary: Material removal on lathe, drill, mill, shaper and grinder; cutting speed and material-removal rate.

topics.label: CNC Machining
topics.summary: Computer-controlled machine tools: components, axes, G/M codes, closed-loop control.

topics.label: Additive Manufacturing (3-D Printing)
topics.summary: Building parts layer by layer from a CAD model: process chain, technologies, applications.

topics.label: Thermal Engineering & the IC Engine
topics.summary: Heat engines, four-stroke and two-stroke engines, SI vs CI, compression ratio, Otto efficiency, brake power.

topics.label: Power Plants
topics.summary: Steam (thermal), hydro, nuclear and gas-turbine plants and how each converts energy.

topics.label: Refrigeration & Air Conditioning
topics.summary: Vapour-compression cycle, COP, tonnage and what an air conditioner does.

topics.label: Fuel Cells & Sustainable Energy
topics.summary: Hydrogen fuel cell operation; solar, wind and other renewable technologies.

topics.label: Mechanisms: Four-Bar & Hexapod
topics.summary: Links, pairs, degrees of freedom, Grashof's law and the inversions of the four-bar chain; the hexapod.

topics.label: Mechanical Components & Motion Control
topics.summary: Gears, belts, chains, cams, bearings, couplings, clutches, brakes and rotary-to-linear conversion.

topics.label: Introduction to Robotics & Automation
topics.summary: Robot anatomy, DOF, configurations, sensors and actuators, simple kinematics, levels of automation.

topics.label: Pneumatic & Hydraulic Actuators
topics.summary: Pascal's law, cylinders and force, and how pneumatic and hydraulic systems compare.

modules.title: Bio-Inspired Design in Engineering
modules.desc: Biomimicry and its core ideas, case studies (Velcro, self-healing, termite-mound ventilation, insect-inspired drones and soft robots, neural networks).

topics.label: Introduction to bio-inspired design (Dr Shankar)
topics.summary: Definition, what does and does not count, Rawling's spectrum (biomimetics–biomimicry–bionics), history and the four primitive design forms.

topics.label: Biomimicry case studies across the animal and plant kingdoms
topics.summary: Animal and plant examples: kingfisher beak, boxfish, tadpole, snake, ear bones, beehive, burdock (Velcro) and skin (self-healing).

topics.label: Termite-mound ventilation in green buildings
topics.summary: How termite mounds ventilate, the stack-effect pressure Δp = gh(ρout − ρin), and how green buildings copy it.

topics.label: Insect-inspired drones, part 1: design of a robotic insect
topics.summary: Reading an insect as a design: head, antenna, wings, abdomen; flapping-wing physics and the Reynolds number.

topics.label: Insect drones part 2: intelligence, swarms and soft robots
topics.summary: Insect intelligence, swarms, soft robots and micro-robots.

topics.label: Neural networks based on the human brain
topics.summary: Biological neuron to artificial neuron; activation functions, network shapes and training.

topics.summary: Summary tables for revision.
